name: trans-Pinene hydrate
evidence: Measured in 6 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.17–1.31% of total volatiles (0.034–0.26mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: trans-Pinene hydrate is a botanical molecule belonging to the terpene family, sharing its structural roots with the familiar pine-scented compounds found in many forests. As a terpene hydrate, it represents one of the many specialized molecules plants create to interact with their environment.
consumer_summary.found_in: In nature, it has been identified in Pimenta racemosa, a tree in the myrtle family commonly known as the West Indian bay tree.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Currently, trans-Pinene hydrate remains an uncharted frontier in natural-product chemistry. With no dedicated studies or clinical trials yet recorded in the available literature (Oxford level 5, none found), it stands as a testament to how many botanical molecules are still waiting to be explored by researchers for their potential biological roles.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: There is currently no recorded evidence (Oxford level 5, none found) for this specific molecule in the available literature.
